description: A minimal loop station worked entirely from triggers: one jack records the loop and plays it, another overdubs onto it

params.text: Empties the loop and stops recording and overdubbing, for as long as it is held down

inputs.text: A rising edge starts recording; the next stops it and starts the loop playing; a third throws that loop away and records a new one
A rising edge starts mixing the incoming signal into the loop as it plays, and the next stops it; it does nothing until a loop has been recorded
Any voltage other than 0V here empties the loop and stops recording and overdubbing

outputs.text: The loop as it plays, or the incoming signal while recording

notes: the red lamp is lit while recording or overdubbing and the green lamp once a loop exists.
an edge is counted only when the jack moves away from exactly 0V, and no further edge until it returns there, so a gate that never falls to zero triggers once and then never again.
overdubbing adds without scaling, so going round the loop again and again builds the level until it clips whatever it feeds.
the loop has no length limit; a long recording keeps taking memory until the loop is cleared.
the loop is not saved with the patch, so reloading gives an empty looper.
